sources.title: ICOMOS: Historical Monuments of Thatta, evaluation (1980)
sources.note: Directly read bilingual evaluation, pages 1 to 2. Samma, Argun and Tarkhan succession; Jam Nizamuddin reign to 1509; later Mughal government 1592 to 1739. Local government gives 1508, so no exact death year is asserted.

sources.title: Sindh Antiquities: Jam Nizamuddin’s Tomb, Makli, Thatta
sources.note: Complete indexed original site description read; direct access unavailable. Use architectural observation and named ruler, not the page’s problematic dynasty-wide dates or essentialist attribution of every motif to a religion.

sources.title: Sindh Antiquities: Tomb of Mubarak Khan, Makli
sources.note: Complete indexed original description read. Entrance inscription AH 895 / 1490, genealogy, graves and mihrab. Possible later completion by Ahmed is explicitly a scholarly proposal; disputed death dates and descent claims not adopted.

sources.title: Archaeological Survey of India HQ: Dada Harir’s Mosque at Asarwa
sources.note: Official ASI institutional post, complete indexed original read: central mihrab inscription dates mosque to 1500, patron’s royal household office, five domed bays and central clerestory. This concerns the mosque, distinct from well dates.

sources.title: James Burgess: The Muhammadan Architecture of Ahmadabad, Part II (1905), chapter II
sources.note: Original ASI survey, printed page 4, chapter Bai Harir’s Wav, Mosque and Tomb; full indexed page read, direct PDF cache miss. Arabic well inscription translated with fruit-bearing trees; Sanskrit 1499 and Arabic 1500 dates discussed, including calendrical discrepancies. Same work as Wikimedia Muhammadan Architecture of Ahmadabad vol.8 pt.2.

sources.title: British Museum: cotton textile As1944,08.4
sources.note: Complete indexed original object record read. Broad date 1500s; probably Gujarat, found/acquired Mondongo, Sulawesi. Vina-playing women, parrots, block printing/resist dye/painting, 502 by 96 cm, old darns and modern patches. No exact production year or itinerary.

sources.title: National Monuments Authority: Bibi Sahib’s Masjid heritage bye-laws, Burhanpur
sources.note: Original government PDF section 3.3, printed page 32, directly returned cache miss but complete indexed original section read. Adil Khan III, Begum Rokeya, broad completion 1520 to 1540, Gujarat influence, Persian and Arabic inscriptions. Broad chronology retained; no claim that modern courtyard surfacing or later Mughal waterworks existed in 1500.

sources.title: Ursula Sims-Williams: A samosa recipe and other delights from the Ni‘matnamah (2016)
sources.note: Directly read republication of British Library curator’s original 21 November 2016 post. BL IO Islamic 149; Ghiyas al-Din and Nasir Shah, undated composite production around 1500. Recipes cited from Norah Titley’s facsimile/translation, pages 4 and 17. Treat this, the original BL blog and reused recipe translations as one work for attribution.

sources.title: Vivek Gupta: Images for Instruction, Muqarnas 38 (2021), pages 77 to 112
sources.note: Directly read author PDF. Text 1468 to 1469, illustrated BL Or 3299 circa 1490, pre-window context. Pages 85 to 88 discuss letter guides and toys: hobbyhorse f.220b, top f.212a. Body calls latter spinning top; figure 14 caption calls it yo-yo, so public text uses only hobbyhorse to avoid that inconsistency. DOI 10.1163/22118993-00381P04 and Brill/UCL mirrors grouped.

sources.title: Vivek Gupta: Routes of Translation, South Asian Studies 39.2 (2023), pages 207 to 228
sources.note: Full indexed original article and PDF passages read; direct publisher open unavailable. Introduction: earliest BL Or 13718 copy 1508 for Nasir Shah; paragraph with note 50: checked the following year, and exact scholarly transcription/translation ṣaḥīḥ ast ghalaṭ nīst. Association of marginal note with verifier is an inference from handwriting, not a signed date. No independent visual decipherment claimed.

sources.title: Deccan Heritage Foundation: Rehabilitation of Bidar’s qanat/karez
sources.note: Original conservation project directly read. Fifteenth-century system adapted to local geology; sloping tunnels and access shafts. Waste filters and household collection belong to modern conservation; its planning phase ran from 2016 to 2018. These must not be projected backward. Bidar lies outside this exact polygon.

proposedOverrides.name: Islamic states
proposedOverrides.summary: An atlas umbrella for several distinct regional courts and communities around 1500 to 1530.

batchIdentityNotes.geometry: Sind/Makran western block, Gujarat block, central/eastern Deccan block. Point checks include Thatta, Ahmedabad, Champaner and Burhanpur; exclude Mandu, Bidar, Golconda and Jaunpur. All neighbouring comparisons publicly located.
batchIdentityNotes.related: Keep gujarat, bengal, bahmani-kingdom, delhi-sultanate, ahmadnagar, golkonda and early kingdom-of-sind separate. No shared identity with Hindu states or religious population-wide claim.
batchIdentityNotes.limits: Court recipes and elite books are unusually detailed surviving evidence but do not describe all households. Textiles dated 1500s and mosque completion 1520 to 1540 partly extend beyond 1530. Local historical chronology must not be inferred from the umbrella interval.
